data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The resolution lies in an evolutionary epistemology where corroboration functions as a selection mechanism analogous to natural selection; the preference is defensible not as an inductive inference of truth, but as a pragmatic necessity to act on the currently 'fittest' hypothesis.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the evolutionary analogy fails to explain why we expect the 'fittest' theory to work in novel domains (the problem of projectibility).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the selection pressure (testing) is not truly independent of the theory's content.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Evolutionary Selection: Theories are conjectures (mutations). Severe tests are environmental pressures. Corroboration is the record of survival. We prefer the corroborated theory not because we induce it is true or probable, but because it is the only one that has not been eliminated by the environment. This is a non-inductive, biological analogy: we don't induce a gazelle will survive tomorrow because it survived yesterday; we simply note it is currently the fittest available. The cost is abandoning the idea that science converges on truth in a probabilistic sense, accepting instead a progression of error elimination.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
